newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine inflation seen slightly short of target.
newsitem.headline: Philippine inflation seen slightly short of target.

text.p: Philippine inflation slid again in August and analysts said on Wednesday they expect the trend to continue, although the rate is likely to end the year slightly above the government's target.

"September and October will have lower inflation figures, and in November and December the inflation levels may slightly increase as consumption picks up," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn.
"We are expecting a bumper harvest that will bring about 5.0 percent or 4.5 percent September inflation level," he said.
The National Statistics Office reported on Thursday that August inflation slowed to 7.9 percent year-on-year from 8.9 percent in July.
Analysts said the August rate was within expectations.
The drop in the inflation rate of the food, beverage and tobacco sector by 1.9 percentage points and a 0.3 percentage point decrease in the fuel, light and water sector contributed to the decline.

"We are still on track and we are looking at a September level of 5.0 percent, the lowest for the year simply because of the high year-on-year base September last year and stable prices," Spencer Yap, senior investment analyst at BPI Capital, said.
Inflation peaked to 11.3 percent last September when food shortages shored up prices.
The Philippine government has projected an 8.5 percent full-year inflation but analysts said the actual figure is likely to be slightly higher.

"The 8.5 percent full-year target looks formidable, although the figures show the deceleration trend is intact. If the United States and Iraq conflict does not escalate, then 8.9 percent full-year inflation will be likely," said Joey Salceda, research director at SBC Warburg.
A prolonged conflict between the United States and Iraq may spike inflation levels if domestic oil prices move upwards.
"There should be no room for complacency in light of the United States and Iraq conflict and the month-on-month change in prices," Salceda added.
On a month-on-month basis, prices increased by 1.0 percent in August compared to 0.1 percent in July.
